3Q3 f1:10.en: Her hand spread out an adversary upon all things desirable that they will see nations of nations brought to her sanctuary which you commanded not to come in the assembly to
3Q3 f1:10.notes: Uncertain reconstruction of 'assembly' (position 17). Phrase evidence supports 'all things' (positions 5-6), 'they will see nations' (positions 8-9), and 'assembly to' (positions 17-18).

3Q3 f1:11.en: All the people who gasp seeking bread gave their precious ones in food to return a soul. See and look, YHWH, that I was lavish.
3Q3 f1:11.notes: The translation follows the visible transcription and morphology where possible. Phrase evidence informed the rendering of 'seeking bread' and 'return a soul'. The lexical gloss 'be lavish' for 'זוללה' is retained due to lack of contextual constraints. The particle 'כי' is translated as 'that' based on its common usage. The final colon (׃) is omitted as it has no direct English equivalent.

3Q3 f1:12.en: Not to you all who pass by the way, look and see if there is pain like my pain which was dealt to me, YHWH thrust away in the day of his burning anger.
3Q3 f1:12.notes: The phrase 'like my pain' is uncertain due to damaged text. The phrase 'YHWH thrust away' is a reconstruction of a damaged verb. The phrase 'the day of his burning anger' is supported by repeated phrase evidence.

3Q3 f2:1.en: They hunted as a bird enemies in vain. They were silent in a cistern of the living and praised a stone in. Waters flowed upon my head. I said, I was cut off.
3Q3 f2:1.notes: The translation follows the visible transcription and morphology where possible. The phrase 'a stone in' is supported by repeated phrase evidence. The verb 'hunt' is reconstructed but supported by the visible form. The translation conservatively preserves all recoverable lexical items and their order, without adding unlicensed subjects or connectors.

3Q3 f2:2.en: I called your name, Yahweh, from a pit of lowest parts. My sound was heard: do not hide your ear to my relief, to my cry. You approached on the day I would call out; you said, 'Do not fear.'
3Q3 f2:2.notes: Positions 7, 17, and 25 are untranslatable punctuation. Position 9 is reconstructed and uncertain.

3Q3 f2:3.en: You have contended, my Lord, the law-case of my soul; you have redeemed my life. See, YHWH, my oppression; judge my justice. You have seen all vengeance, all their designs to me.
3Q3 f2:3.notes: The translation follows visible morphology and repeated phrase evidence where available. Uncertainty arises from reconstruction at positions 1 and 8, and an unknown lemma at position 7. The phrase 'all their designs to me' is supported by repeated phrase evidence, though 'designs to' is a paraphrase of the literal 'thoughts to'.

3Q3 f2:4.en: You have heard, reproach of YHWH, all their plans upon us. Their lips will rise, and their groaning upon all the day.
3Q3 f2:4.notes: The phrase 'upon us' is inferred from the suffix on 'upon' (position 6), though the antecedent is unclear. The phrase 'their lips will rise' is a reconstruction of the damaged text at position 8, with 'lips' being a plausible restoration given the context. The phrase 'upon all the day' is a common expression, supported by repeated phrase evidence.
